questions.q: What is the past infinitive of « voir » ?
choices: avoir vu
être vu
ayant vu
avoir voir
questions.why: Avoir or être in the infinitive, plus the past participle. Voir takes avoir, so avoir vu: to have seen.
Après is always followed by the past infinitive. Après manger does not exist in French.

choices: Avant de manger, je me lave les mains.
Avant d'avoir mangé, je me lave les mains.
Avant manger, je me lave les mains.
Avant que manger, je me lave les mains.
questions.why: Avant de takes the plain infinitive, and après takes the past infinitive. That asymmetry is the whole trap.

questions.q: Après s'être ___ (lever), elle a pris une douche.
questions.why: Reflexive verbs use être, and here se is the direct object, so the participle agrees with the feminine subject: levée.
With être the participle agrees with the subject even inside an infinitive, so feminine plural: parties.

questions.q: Which pair of meanings is right?
choices: Je suis content de venir = I'm glad I came; je suis content d'être venu = I'm glad to be coming
Je suis content de venir = I'm glad to be coming; je suis content d'être venu = I'm glad I came
Both mean exactly the same thing
Only the first is grammatical
questions.why: The past infinitive shifts the action backwards. The plain infinitive stays at the same time as the main verb, or later.

questions.q: Translate: I regret having said that. → Je regrette ___ dit ça.
questions.why: Any verb or preposition that takes an infinitive can take the past infinitive when the action is earlier. Regretter takes de, which elides before avoir.

questions.q: Which word order is correct for « I'm having my car repaired » ?
choices: Je fais ma voiture réparer.
Je fais réparer ma voiture.
Je fais ma voiture à réparer.
Je réparer fais ma voiture.
questions.why: Faire and its infinitive never separate; the object comes after both. This is the exact opposite of the English order, where the object sits in the middle.

questions.q: Build the sentence: He made me laugh.
questions.why: The pronoun goes before faire, not between faire and the infinitive. Never il a fait moi rire.
Fait followed by an infinitive is invariable, always. Compare je les ai faits, with no infinitive, where it does agree.
Voir, entendre and laisser do agree when the preceding pronoun is the subject of the infinitive. Faire is the one verb that never agrees.

questions.q: Elle s'est ___ couper les cheveux. — she had her hair cut.
questions.why: Se faire plus infinitive means something was done to you. And fait before an infinitive stays invariable even here.

questions.q: « J'ai fait réparer la voiture ___ un mécanicien. » Which preposition, and why?
choices: à — the doer always takes à
par — the emphasis is on who performed the work
de — after a causative faire
pour — the mechanic benefits
questions.why: À is for a person you are directing (faire lire un livre à un enfant); par when the point is who did it, and it also removes the ambiguity à can create.

questions.say: Après avoir mangé, je suis sorti.
questions.q: Type what you hear, in correct written French.
a: Après avoir mangé, je suis sorti.
Après avoir mangé je suis sorti
Après avoir mangé, je suis sorti
questions.why: Après plus past infinitive, same subject throughout. The comma marks the boundary between the two clauses.

questions.q: Say this out loud: I'm having my car repaired.
questions.why: Faire plus infinitive, with the object after both verbs. Nothing may come between fais and réparer.
